- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% for the first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is high (≥0.7), model tends to overreact with sharp upward moves; dampen forecast momentum by 10–15% in the first 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3), model underestimates downward moves; increase forecast by 1–3% for the first 3–5 days to account for mean reversion.
- After a price spike, model often overshoots the true decline; apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 5–10% for the next 3–5 days post-spike.
- Model exhibits strong lag in capturing sentiment shifts; if sentiment drops sharply, adjust forecast 2–3 days ahead to reflect the new trend direction.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate the final 5–7 days; add 0.5–1.5% to the last 5–7 forecast values to account for mean reversion or short-term volatility.
